inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,455 logical lines. The paper builds a lower bound for critical-line and simple zeros by converting derivative-combination symmetry into an argument-counting problem, bounding that count through a mollified second moment, evaluating the moment through shifted means and contour transforms, and making the longer mollifier admissible through averaged Kloosterman-sum estimates. The text layer is coherent at the prose/mechanism level but many displayed formulas are damaged or absent, so exact formula transcription and numerical reproduction require scan verification.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the two-fifths goal, the longer-mollifier innovation, the three-paper synthesis, and the coefficient/derivative freedom to be optimized.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Background material and Statement of theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recalls standard zeta background, defines the critical-line proportions, records earlier bounds, and states the paper's quantitative theorem.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Beginning of the proof
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Turns critical-line zeros into changes of argument of a symmetry-compatible derivative combination, introduces its polynomial differential-operator approximation and mollifier, and reduces both total and simple-zero bounds to a mollified mean square.

sections_inspected.label: 4. The mean value theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the decisive mean-square asymptotic, derives the variational problem for the mollifier polynomial, and records parameter choices yielding the numerical bounds.

sections_inspected.label: 5. The proposition
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces a shifted generating integral and derives the target derivative-weighted mean by analyticity and Cauchy differentiation.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Initial Lemmas
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Separates the arithmetic mollifier sum from the analytic shifted integral and uses an antisymmetry identity to assemble the proposition.

sections_inspected.label: 7. The main term
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses smoothing, an Estermann-type functional equation, Mellin inversion, localization, contour shifts, and residues to identify the main term.

sections_inspected.label: 8. The error terms and note added in proof
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Dyadically decomposes the off-diagonal errors, applies averaged Kloosterman bounds after Vaughan decomposition, treats a complementary range with Weil's bound, and records a slight numerical improvement.

sections_inspected.label: References and publication back matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliography and publication metadata; no new source-depth unit.

accepted_units.title: Longer mollifier enabled by averaged Kloosterman control
accepted_units.why_material: The paper identifies the move from mollifier exponent one-half to four-sevenths as the new ingredient and decomposes the proof into mean-square reduction, arithmetic main-term evaluation, and Kloosterman error control.
accepted_units.context_note: The full introductory paragraph and its three-paper division of labor are included; no external paper is needed to recover the claimed architecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula risk: the exponents and division of labor are recoverable from prose, but the displayed mollifier itself is not in this span.

accepted_units.title: Coefficient and derivative-combination freedom deferred to optimization
accepted_units.why_material: The source contrasts a fixed Levinson mollifier with polynomially weighted coefficients chosen by calculus of variations and simultaneously enlarges the initial derivative combination, exposing two independent design freedoms.
accepted_units.context_note: This exact span repairs the v1 unit's missing bounds and includes both the polynomial boundary conditions and the prose describing the generalized combination.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula risk: several displayed definitions are lost in extraction; the optimization freedoms and boundary conditions are prose-recoverable, but exact coefficient formulas require the scan.

accepted_units.title: Critical-line and simple-zero proportion theorem
accepted_units.why_material: The span defines the proportions being bounded, distinguishes simple critical-line zeros from all critical-line zeros, situates prior bounds, and states the quantitative 0.4077 and 0.401 conclusions.
accepted_units.context_note: Standard zeta continuation and functional-equation material before line 139 is not needed to understand the result labels used here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low-to-moderate: definitions and decimal bounds are legible in prose, though some displayed ratios are extraction-damaged.

accepted_units.title: From derivative symmetry to zeros through change of argument
accepted_units.why_material: Parity on the critical line is used to construct a derivative combination whose real-part zeros detect xi zeros, after which rotations of its argument supply a lower bound for those real-part zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the symmetry conditions, construction intent, target count, and the elementary argument-change bridge.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate-to-high: the exact displayed definition of eta is missing, but the parity constraints and logical bridge are explicit in prose; scan verification is needed for coefficients.

accepted_units.title: Compressing the derivative combination into a polynomial differential operator
accepted_units.why_material: Factoring off the functional-equation factor and using derivative asymptotics turns a finite derivative combination into V(s)=Q((1/L)d/ds)zeta(s), with a symmetry constraint on Q that preserves the critical-line real-part condition.
accepted_units.context_note: The span retains the transition from eta to V1 and then to the usable approximation V, including normalization and symmetry prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: several equations defining V1, Q, and its constraint are only partly extracted; the operator viewpoint is recoverable, while exact identities require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Reducing zero density to a mollified second moment
accepted_units.why_material: The argument principle counts zeros of the auxiliary function, a polynomial mollifier shifts the counting line, and Littlewood's lemma plus arithmetic-geometric mean bounds the zero count by the logarithm of a mollified mean square.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Q normalization, zero-count convention, mollifier length and boundary behavior, shifted line, and resulting lower-bound template.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula risk: the displayed inequalities are damaged, but the sequence of reductions and parameter roles is clear in prose; exact constants require the scan.

accepted_units.title: Specializing the auxiliary function to certify simple zeros
accepted_units.why_material: The source isolates auxiliary-function zeros on the half-line that are not eta zeros and shows that an additional identity forces them to correspond to simple xi zeros, yielding a parallel lower bound with Q restricted to degree one.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes the counted set, the simple-zero implication, and the extra restriction on Q.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the decisive identity and final displayed bound are extraction-damaged; only the implication stated in prose is safely recoverable without the scan.

accepted_units.title: Mean-square asymptotic at mollifier length below four-sevenths
accepted_units.why_material: The paper declares that, apart from numerical calculation, its main theorem follows from a mean-value asymptotic for the mollified differential transform V when the mollifier exponent is below four-sevenths.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the analytic bottleneck statement used by the preceding zero-density reduction and the following optimization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the central displayed asymptotic and its main-term functional are largely absent from the text layer; theorem scope and the theta threshold are prose-legible, but the formula must be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Euler-Lagrange optimization of the mollifier profile
accepted_units.why_material: After fixing the auxiliary polynomial data, the mean-square constant becomes a quadratic functional of P; Euler-Lagrange equations give a boundary-value ODE, and integration by parts reduces its value to boundary data.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes definition of the coefficient integrals, the ODE and boundary conditions, the closed-form solution discussion, and substitution back into the objective.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: enough equations survive to identify the variational mechanism, but several definitions and the full solution formula are damaged; numerical or symbolic reuse requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Parameter choices converting the optimized mean into stated proportions
accepted_units.why_material: For the simple-zero case the source restricts Q to a one-parameter form, evaluates the resulting integrals and variational constant, and records choices producing 0.4013, while a richer Q produces 0.4077.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a parameter certificate rather than a derivation of the mean-value theorem; it closes the numerical step announced at line 401.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the exact Q definition is missing and some parameter glyphs are corrupt; the reported choices and outcomes are legible, but reproduction requires the scan.

accepted_units.title: Shifted zeta integral as a generator for the target mean
accepted_units.why_material: A two-shift proposition packages mollifier products and shifted zeta factors into an analytic function g; applying the proposition and Cauchy's formula in the shift variables recovers the derivative-weighted mean required by Theorem 2.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the proposition's uniformity, the contour representation of V, analyticity in both shifts, and the differentiation step.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: much of the proposition's displayed main term and contour integrand is missing; the generating-function method is prose-recoverable, while exact formulas require the scan.

accepted_units.title: Factoring the shifted proposition into arithmetic and analytic lemmas
accepted_units.why_material: The proposition is split into an asymptotic for a mollifier coefficient sum and an analytic evaluation of g; an antisymmetry identity for the arithmetic main term then cancels the unwanted shifted contribution.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the two lemmas, the cited order-of-summation mechanism for the arithmetic sum, and the identity used to recombine them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the main displayed formulas are incomplete, though the factorization, order change, and cancellation logic are explicit; scan verification is necessary for exact use.

accepted_units.title: Gaussian smoothing as an exact transform step
accepted_units.why_material: A preparatory lemma converts the smoothed contour expression by a change of variables to a known integral identity, setting up the main-term analysis with controlled localization.
accepted_units.context_note: Kept separate from the Estermann functional equation because its role is the smoothing kernel rather than arithmetic duality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the displayed statement is mostly lost; only the change-of-variables role and cited transform are recoverable without the scan.

accepted_units.title: Estermann functional equation and Mellin conversion of the off-diagonal sum
accepted_units.why_material: The additive-twist Dirichlet series is continued and given a functional equation, then Mellin inversion and a contour move turn the exponentially smoothed double sum into dual Estermann terms.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definition of D, its functional-equation provenance, the smoothed sum S, and the full proof strategy for the Mellin transformation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the functional equation's factors are partially corrupt, but the series, duality, contour move, and two dual terms are recognizable; exact normalization requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Uniform localization of the smoothing contour near its singular point
accepted_units.why_material: After deforming to a real-axis contour with an indentation, rescaling around the singular point gives uniform convergence and a residue evaluation of the localized integral.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof retains the path deformation, small-variable comparison, uniformity claim, rescaling, and residue conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the integral statement and some kernels are damaged, while the localization and residue mechanism is prose-legible; exact asymptotic requires the scan.

accepted_units.title: Functional equation, contour splitting, and residue extraction of the main term
accepted_units.why_material: The proof shifts the defining contour, discards a localized residue, applies zeta's functional equation, splits into two rays, invokes the Estermann transform, and uses the localization lemma to show the two M terms reproduce the claimed main term.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the transition from g to the double sums, decomposition into M, R, and E pieces, and the identification of both main contributions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: many displayed integrals are corrupt, but the ordered contour/functional-equation/residue pipeline and equality of the two main contributions are explicit; exact reconstruction needs the scan.

accepted_units.title: Dyadic off-diagonal reduction and the matched analytic/arithmetic bounds
accepted_units.why_material: The remainder is organized by gcd and dyadic N,U,V ranges; the contour is chosen according to whether UV exceeds TN, and separate kernel and exponential-sum lemmas combine to make the total error negligible under the stated length restrictions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes disposal of the R term, definitions of the dyadic sums, the conditional contour move and residue, Lemmas 7 and 8, and their final aggregation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the bounds contain damaged exponents and symbols; the case split and error-budget architecture are recoverable, but exact admissible inequalities require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Separability plus Vaughan's identity decomposes the Möbius-weighted sum
accepted_units.why_material: The gcd variable and smooth weights are separated, Vaughan's identity rewrites the Möbius coefficient into three structured pieces, and each resulting sum is routed to a different estimation strategy.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes separability properties, the identity and coefficient definitions, the S1/S2/S3 split, the common target bound, and the regrouping that prepares S1 for a Kloosterman estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: several coefficient formulas are partially extracted, but the decomposition and routing logic are clear; exact identities should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Averaged Kloosterman bound and exponent bookkeeping for the hard range
accepted_units.why_material: A Deshouillers-Iwaniec lemma controls the multilinear Kloosterman family; the proof then reduces its bound to finitely many exponent tuples and checks the positive and negative exponent cases, exposing the length restriction needed for the longer mollifier.
accepted_units.context_note: The one-line overlap with the preceding unit preserves the transition from regrouped S1 to the external averaged bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the lemma statement and several exponent expressions are extraction-damaged, though the finite-case bookkeeping and thresholds are visible; exact inequalities require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Spectral average in one range, pointwise Weil bound in the complementary range
accepted_units.why_material: For the third Vaughan piece the proof splits on the factor size: the large-factor range reuses the averaged lemma, while the small-factor range sums first and applies Weil's pointwise Kloosterman bound plus partial summation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the factor-size dichotomy, derivative control used in summation by parts, the resulting comparison, and closure of the lemma and theorems.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: displayed sums are incomplete, but the range split and choice of bounds are explicit in prose; constants and exponents require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Post-proof numerical improvement without a new analytic mechanism
accepted_units.why_material: The note records a new auxiliary polynomial and parameter value that slightly improves the all-critical-line proportion to 0.4088, showing that the analytic framework admits later numerical retuning.
accepted_units.context_note: Kept as a distinct update because it changes the reported numerical certificate but not the preceding proof architecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the polynomial and improved bound are legible, but one parameter glyph is missing and should be checked against the scan before reproduction.
